newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ski resort officials convicted in avalanche.
newsitem.headline: French ski resort officials convicted in avalanche.

text.p: Two French ski resort officials were convicted of manslaughter by negligence and given suspended jail terms on Thursday over an 1996 avalanche which killed a skier.

Christian Reverbel and Andre Roderon, in charge of the safety of ski pistes at the l'Alpe-d'Huez resort, were given six-month suspended sentences over the death of 35-year-old Dominique Assedat in a snow-slide on January 1, 1996.
The court ruled that the officials had acted negligently in opening the piste on the Sarenne glacier to skiers on a day when there was a high avalanche risk.

They had also failed to take measurements of the snow depth, which an expert witness told the court was a basic precaution, and had not used explosives to cause controlled avalanches of dangerous snow before opening the runs, the court found.
Two other officials were acquitted in the case. The resort's management company was fined 250,000 francs ($44,000) and ordered to pay 100,000 francs ($17,500) in damages to the victim's family.
